zh.title: 谷胱甘肽：了解抗氧化作用与肤色护理的证据
zh.summary: 谷胱甘肽是一种人体能够自行合成的三肽，是人体抗氧化防御系统的一部分。

blocks.text: 谷胱甘肽（Glutathione）是一种人体能够自行合成的物质，由谷氨酸、半胱氨酸和甘氨酸三种氨基酸组成，属于三肽。它广泛存在于细胞中，是人体抗氧化防御系统的一部分。
在护肤领域，谷胱甘肽常被用于抗氧化和肤色管理相关产品。不过，它在人体内的重要作用，并不代表额外涂抹、口服或注射后，一定能够获得明显的美容效果。不同使用途径的证据和风险，需要分别看待。
一、谷胱甘肽与皮肤有什么关系？
参与抗氧化防御
人体正常代谢，以及紫外线等外界因素，都可能产生自由基和其他活性氧。当这些物质超过身体的调节能力时，便可能形成氧化应激，影响细胞和组织。
谷胱甘肽参与细胞内的氧化还原反应，帮助维持正常的细胞环境。它有两种相互关联的形式：
可能影响部分色素形成过程
谷胱甘肽受到肤色护理领域关注，与其抗氧化作用及可能影响黑色素形成的机制有关。研究提出的机制包括影响酪氨酸酶相关活性及黑色素合成过程。
但**机制上的可能性，不等于已经证明能够稳定、明显或永久地改变肤色**。临床评价还需要看实际使用配方、研究人群、观察时间及效果大小。
二、外用谷胱甘肽有哪些研究？
一项纳入 **30 名健康女性、持续 10 周**的随机双盲半脸对照研究，比较了含 **2% 氧化型谷胱甘肽**的乳液与不含该成分的对照乳液。
研究观察到，使用谷胱甘肽的一侧，黑色素指数有所下降；部分皮肤含水量、平滑度及细纹指标也出现变化，研究期间未报告明显不良反应。
这些结果提供了初步依据，但需要了解其局限：

items: 样本量较小，观察时间较短。
研究对象是特定年龄范围的健康女性。
测试的是具体配方，不能代表所有谷胱甘肽护肤品。
仪器指标的变化，不一定等于肉眼可见的明显改善。
短期内未发现明显问题，不能证明长期使用或所有人群都没有风险。

blocks.text: 因此，比较客观的表述是：**部分外用配方显示了改善色素指标及皮肤状态的潜力，但仍需要更充分、独立且长期的研究。**
三、可以改善暗沉、痘印或黄褐斑吗？
这些问题不能混为一谈。

head: 皮肤问题
需要考虑的因素
rows: 可能与干燥、皮肤纹理、日晒或色素有关
红色痘印与褐色色素沉着的机制不同
常涉及日晒、激素及其他因素，需要长期管理
应先明确性质，尤其是新出现或持续变化的斑点

blocks.text: 现有小型研究不能支持谷胱甘肽能够治疗所有色斑，也不足以保证消除痘印或黄褐斑。**健康肤色本身不是疾病，护理目标应以减少异常色素沉着、改善均匀度和维持皮肤健康为主。**
四、怎样加入日常护肤？
如果选择外用产品，应遵循说明，先在小范围试用，再逐步扩大使用范围。初次使用时可降低频率，并避免同时更换多款产品。
一般护理顺序可以是：
**温和洁面 → 精华或乳液 → 保湿 → 白天防晒**
具体顺序取决于产品类型。谷胱甘肽不是防晒成分，不能替代广谱防晒、遮阳和衣物保护。
与 VC、烟酰胺或 A 醇搭配时，也应以完整配方和耐受情况为依据，不必为了“加强抗氧化”而层层叠加。
谷胱甘肽参与正常细胞代谢，并不等于额外使用可以带来所谓的“全身排毒”。
同样，抗氧化作用不能直接换算为明确的抗衰老年限或可保证的美容效果。
**谷胱甘肽是人体抗氧化系统中的重要物质。部分外用和口服研究显示了肤色护理方面的潜力，但证据仍有限，应避免将初步发现扩大为确定的疗效承诺。**
本文仅供一般皮肤健康科普，不代替个体化诊断或治疗建议。

en.title: Glutathione: understanding its antioxidant role and the evidence for skin tone care
en.summary: Glutathione is a tripeptide that the body can make itself, and it is part of the body’s antioxidant defence system.

blocks.text: Glutathione is a substance the body can make itself. It is made up of three amino acids, glutamic acid, cysteine and glycine, which makes it a tripeptide. It is found widely in cells and is part of the body’s antioxidant defence system.

In skincare, glutathione is often used in products related to antioxidant care and skin tone management. However, its important role inside the body does not mean that additionally applying it to the skin, taking it by mouth or having it injected will necessarily produce a noticeable cosmetic effect. The evidence and risks for each route of use need to be considered separately.
1. How is glutathione related to the skin?
Taking part in antioxidant defence

Normal metabolism in the body, as well as external factors such as ultraviolet (UV) radiation, can produce free radicals and other reactive oxygen species. When these exceed the body’s capacity to regulate them, oxidative stress may develop, affecting cells and tissues.
Glutathione takes part in redox reactions within cells, helping to maintain a normal cellular environment. It exists in two interrelated forms:
Possibly affecting some pigment-forming processes

Glutathione has attracted attention in skin tone care because of its antioxidant effects and mechanisms that may influence melanin formation. Mechanisms proposed in research include effects on tyrosinase-related activity and on the process of melanin synthesis.

But **a possible mechanism is not the same as proof that it can change skin colour reliably, noticeably or permanently**. Clinical evaluation also needs to look at the formulation actually used, the study population, the length of observation and the size of the effect.
2. What research is there on topical glutathione?
A randomised, double-blind, split-face controlled study of **30 healthy women over 10 weeks** compared a lotion containing **2% oxidised glutathione** with a control lotion that did not contain it.

The study observed a decrease in the melanin index on the side treated with glutathione; some measures of skin moisture, smoothness and fine lines also changed, and no significant adverse reactions were reported during the study.
These results provide preliminary evidence, but their limitations need to be understood:

items: The sample was small and the observation period short.
The participants were healthy women within a specific age range.
A specific formulation was tested, so the results cannot represent all glutathione skincare products.
Changes in instrument measurements do not necessarily equal an obvious improvement visible to the naked eye.
Not finding obvious problems in the short term does not prove that long-term use, or use in every population, is free of risk.

blocks.text: So a more objective statement would be: **some topical formulations have shown potential to improve pigment measures and skin condition, but more thorough, independent and long-term research is still needed.**
3. Can it improve dullness, acne marks or melasma?
These concerns should not be lumped together.

head: Skin concern
Factors to consider
rows: May be related to dryness, skin texture, sun exposure or pigment
Red acne marks and brown pigmentation arise through different mechanisms
Often involves sun exposure, hormones and other factors; needs long-term management
Their nature should be clarified first, especially spots that are new or keep changing

blocks.text: Existing small studies cannot support the idea that glutathione can treat all dark spots, nor are they enough to guarantee the removal of acne marks or melasma. **Healthy skin colour is not a disease in itself; the main goals of care should be to reduce abnormal pigmentation, improve evenness and maintain skin health.**
4. How can you add it to your daily skincare?

If you choose a topical product, follow the instructions, try it on a small area first, then gradually widen the area of use. When starting out, you can use it less often, and avoid changing several products at the same time.
A general order of use could be:
**Gentle cleanser → serum or lotion → moisturiser → sunscreen (daytime)**
The exact order depends on the product type. Glutathione is not a sunscreen ingredient and cannot replace broad-spectrum sunscreen, shade and protective clothing.

When combining it with vitamin C, niacinamide or retinol, also base your choices on the full formulations and your tolerance; there is no need to pile on layer after layer to “boost antioxidant effects”.
Glutathione’s part in normal cell metabolism does not mean that using extra glutathione can bring a so-called “whole-body detox”.
Likewise, antioxidant effects cannot be directly converted into a definite number of years of anti-ageing or a guaranteed cosmetic result.

**Glutathione is an important substance in the body’s antioxidant system. Some topical and oral studies have shown potential for skin tone care, but the evidence is still limited, and preliminary findings should not be stretched into definite promises of effectiveness.**
This article is for general skin health education only and does not replace individual diagnosis or treatment advice.
